factors.name: Pace & Transition
factors.desc: How often possessions end in early-clock / transition shots (after steals, rebounds and even made baskets) versus long, late-clock half-court possessions.

loadings.label: Early-clock fouls drawn per poss (pressure proxy)

factors.name: Ball Movement
factors.desc: Share of made baskets that are assisted, at the rim, from mid-range and from three. Low = isolation / one-on-one creation.

factors.name: Shot Diet
factors.desc: Where the jump shots come from: the 3-point line or 2-point jumpers. Three-heavy teams also tend to crash the glass less.

factors.name: Foul Pressure
factors.desc: How often the offense forces defensive fouls and gets to the line, including early in the shot clock.

loadings.label: Early-clock fouls drawn per poss (pressure proxy)

factors.name: Risk Profile
factors.desc: Turnovers (especially live-ball) plus offensive rebounding and dunks: an aggressive, chaotic offense versus a careful one.

factors.name: Rim Pressure
factors.desc: Share of shots at the rim plus putback frequency, versus jump shots.

archetypes.name: Mid-Range Shot-Makers
archetypes.desc: Lives on 2-point jumpers instead of threes or the rim, and rarely draws fouls. Effective when the shooters are elite, but the shot diet is inefficient on average.
archetypes.history: Missouri State '17 & '20, Houston '25–'26, BYU '17, Southern Miss '20

archetypes.name: Isolation Creators
archetypes.desc: Low assist rate: guards create their own shots, take threes and get to the free-throw line.
archetypes.history: Maryland '15, UCF '17, High Point '24, UNC Wilmington '23, Towson '16–'17

archetypes.name: Grind & Crash
archetypes.desc: Slower, turnover-tolerant offense that makes up for it on the offensive glass and around the rim.
archetypes.history: Saint Mary's '15, Southern Illinois '21, Sacramento State '24, Tarleton State '25

archetypes.name: Inside-Out Motion
archetypes.desc: The most assist-heavy offense, fed through the post. It draws lots of fouls and gets easy looks from interior passing.

archetypes.name: Downhill Rim Attack
archetypes.desc: Gets to the rim relentlessly, at a quicker pace, and follows its misses with putbacks.
archetypes.history: Virginia Tech '16, Rhode Island '20, South Alabama '26, Campbell '26, Stephen F. Austin '21

archetypes.name: Run-and-Gun Bombers
archetypes.desc: Fast pace plus a heavy three-point diet: lots of possessions and lots of threes, with ball movement to find shooters.
archetypes.history: Savannah State '17–'19, The Citadel '18, William & Mary '25–'26, Cal Poly '25, Cornell '22

archetypes.name: Patient Precision
archetypes.desc: Slow, low-turnover half-court offense that works the clock for a good jump shot. Low variance, with few empty possessions.

factors.name: Zone Signature
factors.desc: Share of opponents' baskets that are assisted. Zones give up passes and assisted shots; aggressive man defenses force one-on-one play. The clearest zone fingerprint (Syracuse, Baylor's matchup zone).

loadings.label: Opp. assisted share of makes allowed
Opp. assisted share at rim allowed
Opp. dunk share of FGA allowed
Opp. live-ball turnovers per possession allowed

factors.name: Turnover Pressure
factors.desc: Turnovers forced (live-ball and backcourt/early), usually at the cost of giving up offensive rebounds and dunks.

loadings.label: Opp. live-ball turnovers per possession allowed
Opp. backcourt/early turnovers per poss (press proxy) allowed
Opp. dunk share of FGA allowed
Opp. assisted share at rim allowed
Opp. assisted share of makes allowed

factors.name: Foul Tendency
factors.desc: Defensive fouls and opponent free-throw rate, including reach-in fouls early in the clock.

loadings.label: Opp. defensive fouls drawn per poss allowed
Opp. early-clock fouls drawn per poss (pressure proxy) allowed
Opp. transition shots per possession allowed
Opp. push after defensive rebounds allowed
Opp. putback attempts per OREB allowed
Opp. backcourt/early turnovers per poss (press proxy) allowed

factors.name: Transition Defense
factors.desc: How often opponents get early-clock transition shots, after rebounds, makes or steals.

loadings.label: Opp. transition shots per possession allowed
Opp. push after defensive rebounds allowed
Opp. push after opponent makes allowed

factors.name: Rim vs. Arc
factors.high: Runs shooters off, concedes the rim
factors.desc: Which shots the defense gives up: threes (pack-line style) or rim attempts (extended perimeter coverage).

loadings.label: Opp. putback attempts per OREB allowed
Opp. dunk share of FGA allowed
Opp. assisted share of makes allowed

factors.name: Clock Burn
factors.desc: Length of opponents' possessions and share of late-clock shots forced.

loadings.label: Opp. transition shots per possession allowed
Opp. push after opponent makes allowed
Opp. push after defensive rebounds allowed
Opp. backcourt/early turnovers per poss (press proxy) allowed

factors.name: Mid-Range Funnel
factors.desc: Share of opponent shots that are 2-point jumpers. Drop coverage and help-heavy schemes concede the mid-range to protect the rim and arc.

loadings.label: Opp. putback attempts per OREB allowed
Opp. assisted share of makes allowed

archetypes.name: Denial Man-to-Man
archetypes.desc: Pressures the ball and denies passes: forces turnovers, allows few assisted looks, and makes opponents work deep into the shot clock.
archetypes.history: VCU '19–'22 (Havoc), Virginia '16, Houston '26, Florida State '24, Northern Illinois '15

archetypes.name: Conservative Pack-Line
archetypes.desc: The most common defense. Sits back, protects the paint and concedes threes, forcing few turnovers and allowing few mid-range jumpers.
archetypes.history: Northeastern '15, William & Mary '20, Notre Dame '26, App State '25

archetypes.name: Zone
archetypes.desc: The unmistakable zone fingerprint: opponents' baskets are heavily assisted, with lots of passing around the perimeter.
archetypes.history: Syracuse '16–'23, Baylor '16 (matchup zone), Eastern Michigan '19, Merrimack '23

archetypes.name: Contain, Don't Foul
archetypes.desc: Disciplined and low-foul, but it gives up transition chances and doesn't force turnovers.
archetypes.history: Villanova '17, Toledo '19, Southern Utah '25–'26, North Florida '18–'19

archetypes.name: Full-Court Chaos
archetypes.desc: Pressure everywhere: forces lots of turnovers and fouls, and speeds opponents up.
archetypes.history: West Virginia '15–'18 (Press Virginia), Stephen F. Austin '15–'18, Abilene Christian '22

archetypes.name: Drop & Funnel
archetypes.desc: Takes away the rim and the 3-point line and concedes 2-point jumpers. A classic drop-coverage profile.
archetypes.history: San Diego '16–'19, Missouri State '18–'20, Illinois '22, Seattle U '18

factors.name: Rotation Depth
factors.desc: Effective rotation size, bench minutes and how spread minutes are across lineups.

loadings.label: Share of assists by top playmaker

factors.name: Who Drives It
factors.desc: Share of usage and rebounding by guards versus forwards and centers.

factors.name: Big-Man Type
factors.desc: Minutes to back-to-the-basket centers and power forwards, versus wings and stretch-4s who shoot threes.

factors.name: Frontcourt Size
factors.desc: Height of the main frontcourt players and of the rotation overall.

factors.name: Star Usage
factors.desc: How concentrated usage is in the top player.

loadings.label: Share of assists by top playmaker

archetypes.name: Towering Frontcourt
archetypes.desc: Exceptional size up front, with a big height gap between the frontcourt and the guards.
archetypes.history: Western Kentucky '22–'23, Loyola Marymount '19, Seattle U '18, Youngstown State '25

archetypes.name: Small-Ball Guards
archetypes.desc: Guards carry the usage and the rebounding; undersized, with wings instead of traditional bigs.
archetypes.history: American '15, UMass Lowell '18, Tarleton State '22, Pittsburgh '26

archetypes.name: Deep Platoon
archetypes.desc: Long benches and lots of lineup variety, with no single focal point.

archetypes.name: Forward-Led Positionless
archetypes.desc: Forwards run the offense; skilled, versatile bigs and wings with few traditional centers.

archetypes.name: Star System
archetypes.desc: Offense funneled through one high-usage player.
archetypes.history: Detroit Mercy '23 (Antoine Davis), UNC Greensboro '21, Eastern Washington '17, Fairfield '18

archetypes.name: Traditional Two-Big
archetypes.desc: Old-school frontcourt: back-to-the-basket bigs who rarely shoot threes.
archetypes.history: McNeese '18, California Baptist '24, Boston College '22, Drexel '16

clash.label: Rim attack
clash.why: Rim attempts taken vs. rim attempts the defense concedes

clash.label: Ball security vs. pressure
clash.why: Low turnovers vs. a defense that doesn't force them

clash.label: Transition
clash.why: Pushes the pace vs. lets opponents run

clash.label: Free throws
clash.why: Draws fouls vs. fouls a lot

clash.label: Ball movement
clash.why: Assisted offense vs. allows assisted looks

clash.label: Short mid-range / floaters
clash.why: Lives in the paint/elbows vs. concedes it

clash.label: Pull-up jumpers
clash.why: Pull-up shooting vs. a defense that concedes pull-ups (drop-coverage signature)

clash.label: Corner 3s
clash.why: Corner-three creation vs. corner threes allowed

clash.label: Second-chance finishes
clash.why: Putbacks per offensive board vs. putbacks allowed

clash.label: Shot blocking
clash.why: Avoids blocks vs. a defense that doesn't block shots
